name: Shaniwar Wada Palace
summary: Shaniwarwada is a 13-story fort of the Peshwas of the Maratha Empire, built in 1732. It was the seat of the Peshwas until 1818 when they lost control to the British East India Company.
whyItMatters: Symbol of Maratha military prowess and administrative power during the peak expansion of the Maratha Empire.

name: Lal Mahal
summary: Lal Mahal (Red Palace) is a historic palace established by Shahaji Bhosale for his wife Jijabai and son Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, who spent his early childhood here.
whyItMatters: Site of the daring night attack by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj on Shaista Khan in 1663.

name: Pataleshwar Cave Temple
summary: Pataleshwar Rock-cut Cave Temple is an 8th-century monolithic rock-cut cave carved out of a single basalt rock pillar dedicated to Lord Shiva.
whyItMatters: One of the oldest surviving structural monuments in Pune, showcasing master Rashtrakuta rock engineering.

name: Sinhagad Fort
summary: Sinhagad (Lion's Fort) is an ancient hill fortress located 30km southwest of Pune, renowned for the historic Battle of Sinhagad in 1670.
whyItMatters: Site where warrior Tanaji Malusare recaptured the fort for Shivaji Maharaj using monitor lizards to scale steep cliffs.
